speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain radiates to other areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your story of the finger getting caught and pulled forcefully, that sounds like a significant injury. Did you hear a loud "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and can you still move your finger or make a fist?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mention of pyelonephritis seems inconsistent with your localized finger injury; ignoring that, I see you cannot flex the distal joint and the finger is stuck in extension. This "dropped knuckle" appearance following a lateral pull injury is highly suggestive of an extensor mechanism tear. Did the inability to make a fist start immediately after the injury, or did it develop gradually? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right hand to rule out avulsion fracture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Extensor Mechanism Tear (Mallet Finger) of the Right Ring Finger. The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, combined with the finger resting in extension and a normal X-ray ruling out fracture, confirms a tear of the extensor tendon insertion.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
